episodes.213243: A large thunderstorm complex developed in south central South Dakota in the early morning hours of June 29th and tracked northeast across the state, finally exiting into southeast North Dakota and western Minnesota during the mid morning hours. Extreme winds were observed with this system. Two separate weather sensors recorded extraordinary peak wind gusts of 131 mph: the South Dakota State University mesonet station located at the Highmore Municipal Airport and a personal weather station three miles east-southeast of Holabird. These winds knocked down trees and damaged structures across portions of central and northeast South Dakota. Ground zero was the town of Highmore (population of roughly 650 residents) in Hyde county where up to 80 to 90 percent of residences and commercial buildings experiences some form of wind damage, with a number of vehicles and farm implements also being tipped and tossed.  Residents at Highmore Health, the towns nursing home had to be evacuated due to damage to the facility. There was no loss of human life and injuries reported were due to post-storm cleanup operations. 3 horses died due to these high winds. Cost of debris cleanup in Hyde county alone topped out at 1.4 million dollars. ||Electrical infrastructure was severely disrupted, causing $2.4 million in utility distribution damage across Hyde and Hand counties. Power was knocked out to 1,072 residents in Hyde County (94% of the county). Power generation was heavily impacted; at least 20 wind turbines were damaged or destroyed at the Triple H and North Bend wind farms, with replacement costs estimated at $50 million.||Day County suffered extensive damage, particularly around Andover, where straight-line wind speeds reached 100 mph. Extensive tree stands were leveled, grain bins dented, and buildings damaged at the Andover Threshing Grounds. Day County power damage reached $18,000, leaving 487 residents without electricity. A brief EFU tornado was confirmed near Andover.||Even as the storm system departed, wrap around high winds caused additional tree damage in areas that had just missed out on thunderstorm wind damage, with several trees and limbs down in parts of Aberdeen, and a peak wind gust measured on a personal weather station of 88 mph in the town of Westport (Brown county).||Governor Rhoden requested a Presidential Disaster Declaration to assist with damage cleanup and repairs for Hyde, Hand, Hughes, Buffalo and Stanley counties including Lower Brule and Crow Creek reservations.
episodes.213358: Lightning damaged two homes in North Carolina during the evening hours.
episodes.213463: A line of thunderstorms tracked through northeast Wisconsin ahead of an advancing warm front during the early morning hours on Monday (6/29). The strongest storm produced hail up to half dollar size in far northern Door County.
episodes.213464: A line of thunderstorms produced large hail over the Lake Michigan waters during the early morning hours on Monday (6/29).
episodes.213728: Potent upper level disturbance and jet streak moved eastward over the eastern Plains during the late evening hours of June 28th. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed and tracked northeast over far eastern Wyoming and western Nebraska until 3:00 AM MDT.
episodes.213842: A surface boundary was in the vicinity of the combined Panhandles through the afternoon and evening hours of June 29th. This combined with daytime heating, ample instability and enough dry air in the higher levels of the atmosphere to bring scattered showers and thunderstorms to the region. Some of these storms intensified to be severe with damaging winds being the primary hazard.
episodes.214160: Troughing was evident over the western CONUS on the 28th, and west Texas and southeast New Mexico were under southwesterly flow aloft. Pulses within this flow, coupled with upslope flow and surface convergence on a weak dryline, yielded shower and thunderstorm development starting in the higher terrain and spreading across much of the area. A few thunderstorms managed to produce severe downburst winds.
episodes.214162: Similar to June 28th, pulses in the southwesterly flow aloft coupled with upslope flow yielded shower and thunderstorm development, starting in the higher terrain and spreading northeastward towards the Trans-Pecos and Permian Basin. A few storms produced severe downburst winds.
episodes.214185: A warm and moist environment set up across Eastern North Carolina during the afternoon hours of June Twenty-Eighth. At the same time the seabreeze combined with a surface trough across the Coastal Plain and an incoming cold front to become the focus of scattered shower and thunderstorm activity during the afternoon and evening hours. With this favorable environment in place, a few of these storms became strong to severe in nature bringing a strong and damaging wind threat to the Neuse and Bay Rivers, southern Pamlico Sound, and along the coastal waters south of Ocracoke Island.
episodes.214308: A stationary front just to the south of Philadelphia produced heavy rain across portions of the Delaware Valley.
episodes.214525: On June 29th, 2026, severe weather fueled by record humidity and high temperatures impacted western Lake Superior. Two waves of storms swept through the area, producing damaging wind gusts as high as 57 mph along the South Shore of Lake Superior during the afternoon round of storms.
episodes.214526: On June 29th, 2026, severe weather fueled by record humidity and high temperatures impacted the Duluth County Warning Area, leading to 27 total warnings across northeast Minnesota and northwest Wisconsin. Two waves of severe storms swept through the area, producing golf ball-sized hail (1.75 inches), damaging straight-line wind gusts to 60���65 mph, several reported funnel clouds, and one tornado in central St. Louis County during the overnight round of storms. The severe winds uprooted trees, damaged structures, and knocked down power lines across multiple counties.
episodes.214527: On June 29th, 2026, severe weather fueled by record humidity and high temperatures impacted the Duluth County Warning Area, leading to 27 total warnings across northeast Minnesota and northwest Wisconsin. Two waves of severe storms swept through the area, producing ping pong ball-sized hail (1.50 inches) and damaging straight-line wind gusts to 60 mph. The severe winds uprooted trees, damaged structures, and knocked down power lines across multiple counties.
episodes.214569: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms swept over Lake Superior in late June as minor disturbances pivoted around a mid-level ridge over the southeastern CONUS. These disturbances caused multiple incidences of thunderstorm-driven outflow and gusty winds on Lake Superior from the afternoon of the 29th to the early morning hours of the 30th.  A strengthening low level jet and wake lows trailing the thunderstorms resulted in additional periods of gusty winds, above gale force.
episodes.214617: Large scale upper level troughing with two separate embedded upper level lows progressed across the region late June. The colder core, which actually ended up being the southern of the two, moved across Southwest Montana and resulted in snow levels falling to below 6,000ft at times as heaviest precipitation moved over the area. Heavy snow developed near and above pass level in northwest Beaverhead County, resulting in nearly 2 feet of snow near the peaks close to the ID border.||Meanwhile further north under the second upper low, a strong surface low ended up developing near the Hi-Line, which resulted in strong winds in a few zones before the surface low filled/weakened. ||Strong upper level support further north resulted in widespread heavy rains, with additional upslope forcing along the Rocky Mountain Front, which resulted in some flooding in Glacier NP June 29.
episodes.214751: A weak disturbance within a buoyant environment forced thunderstorms that caused damaging severe winds in Michigan's Upper Peninsula on the 29th.
episodes.214973: Surface low pressure tracked across the Northern Plains, leading to moisture advection and isolated severe thunderstorms across central North Dakota. Supercells developed during the evening hours, continuing until the late evening. The strongest wind gust report was near Minot Air Force Base in Ward County, where a trained spotter reported wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph. The largest hail occurred in McHenry County, with hail of 2 inches in diameter observed near Velva and Drake. A tornado was observed approximately 4 miles east-southeast of Riverdale in McLean County around 9 PM CDT. There was no known damage from this tornado, therefore there is no estimated wind speed and it is assigned a rating of EF-Unknown per NWS policy.
episodes.214974: A low pressure over the Northern Plains, combined with a moist and unstable air mass, led to a conditional threat of severe thunderstorms as an upper level jet streak moved over North Dakota. Thunderstorms developed in the early afternoon along a quasi-stationary surface trough that was placed across central North Dakota. Numerous large hail and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts were reported across southwest and central North Dakota through the afternoon and evening as storms moved through. The largest hail reported was 2.25 inches in diameter in Max in McLean County. The strongest wind gust was also measured in McLean County, with a 77 mph wind gust reported at a US Air Force Weather station just south of Max.
episodes.214987: Wraparound precipitation from a closed low pressure system located east of the Continental Divide sent abundant moisture into the Northern Rockies. Saturated ground conditions from previous rainfall combined with an additional two to four inches of precipitation, resulting in flooding across parts of northwest Montana.
episodes.215029: Supercell storms early in the day dropped large hail and across Oglala Lakota and the Pine Ridge areas. These storms turned into a linear cluster and moved into Todd and Tripp counties where it produced damaging wind gusts with reports of structure damage.
episodes.215274: During the early morning hours a thunderstorm cluster moved into the western part of the Devils Lake Basin producing severe wind and hail. Later in the morning a thunderstorm cluster developed in northeast SD and expanded into a larger complex as it passed into far southeast ND and across west central and northwest MN, where it produced severe wind gusts in southeast ND. As this complex moved east a wake low resulted in non thunderstorm high winds in southeast ND.
episodes.215275: A thunderstorm complex developed during the morning hours in northeast SD and tracked through far southeast ND and across west central MN and parts of northwest MN producing severe thunderstorm winds and large hail. A wake low developed as a result of this MCS with non thunderstorm high winds lingering over parts of west central MN.
episodes.215318: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed across the North Carolina mountains and foothills during the late afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts and hail.
episodes.215319: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon into the early evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215320: Isolated thunderstorms developed over northeast Georgia during the late afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Stephens County.
episodes.215406: During the evening of June 29, 2026, into the early morning hours of June 30, severe thunderstorms moved across northern and eastern Nebraska, producing hail, damaging wind gusts, and a brief tornado. Storms developed along a cold front within a highly unstable air mass characterized by MLCAPE values exceeding 3,500 J/kg, DCAPE values over 1,500 J/kg, and steep lapse rates.||Two distinct rounds of severe weather impacted the area. The first round targeted far northeast Nebraska���primarily Knox and Cedar counties���between 5:00 PM and 8:00 PM CST. This initial round was dominated by a supercell that produced measured wind gusts up to 60 mph and hail up to 1.75 inches in diameter.||A second round of storms developed in east-central Nebraska later in the evening and tracked northeastward. This activity quickly consolidated into a severe convective cluster that produced damaging winds, hail, and a brief tornado as it passed through Boone, Madison, Stanton, and Wayne counties. The complex intensified rapidly upon entering Madison County and the Norfolk area, producing widespread wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph. A personal weather station 2 miles southeast of Hadar recorded a peak gust of 101 mph, which destroyed a well-anchored carport. Multiple hail reports between 1.00 and 2.00 inches in diameter were also received. A brief, EF-0 tornado was also confirmed in Stanton County, with maximum estimated wind speeds of 85 mph. The system continued northeast into the overnight hours, producing severe wind gusts into northwest Iowa and southern Minnesota.
episodes.215708: A hot and humid air mass led to strong destabilization with surface based CAPE near 4000 J/kg in the Central Savannah River Area. While shear was weak, dry air aloft and strong low level lapse rates supported a few storms reaching severe limits.
episodes.215884: A warm southerly flow under high pressure was supportive of strong thunderstorms near the Gulf Stream during overnight hours.
episodes.215885: A weak boundary entering the region along the eastern edge of mid-level ridging encountered an environment displaying large downdraft CAPE and strong mid-level lapse rates, supporting strong thunderstorms across Southeast Georgia.
episodes.215967: Isolated thunderstorms developed along a stationary front during the early evening hours of June 28. Storms intensified into the mid evening hours with hail up to the size of base balls being reported over northern Sheridan County. Severe storms continued through 1 AM MDT on June 29th before lifting north into southern South Dakota.
